speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing dizziness and vertigo; to help me determine the cause, can you tell me if the spinning sensation lasts seconds, minutes, or hours?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Since your vertigo is position-dependent, does it get triggered specifically by turning your head in bed, looking up, or bending down? REQUEST TEST: Dix-Hallpike maneuver.

text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV) of the right posterior canal.

Given the positive Dix-Hallpike maneuver and the presence of right-sided horizontal nystagmus upon position change, I am confident in this diagnosis. Do you have any history of recent head trauma or ear infections?
